la:verb:exquiro.gloss: to seek or seek out, search for or hunt up
senses: to seek or seek out, search for or hunt up
la:verb:exquiro.html:
ex-quīro (in Plautus also exquaero, Bacch. 4, 4, 70 al.), sīvi, sītum, 3, v. a.,
to search out diligently, to seek for; to make inquiry, to inquire, to ask (syn.: requiro, inquiro, investigo, perscrutor; freq. and class.): cum ex te causas divinationis exquirerem,: a te nihildum certi exquiro,; cf.: sed haec non nimis exquiro a Graecis, to ask

of, expect from, : ancillas dedo, quolibet cruciatu exquire,: exquisiturum se vel fidiculis de Caesonia sua, cur, etc.,that he would search out even by the rack,: idem ego dicam, si me exquiret miles,: secum et cum aliis, quid in eo peccatum sit, exquirunt,: omissis auctoritatibus ipsa re ac ratione exquirere veritatem,: sententias,: locum,: sceleratum frigus,to find out,: verum,to search into, investigate,; : facta alicujus ad antiquae religionis rationem,; cf.: verba exquisita ad sonum,: rationes agitare et exquirere,: itinere exquisito per Divitiacum,having ascertained the route, et saep.: exquire de Blesamio, numquid ad regem contra dignitatem tuam scripserit,inquire respecting Blesamius,; cf.: de Varrone tam diligenter,: eis senatus arbitratur singularis exquirendos honores,to devise, invent,.—Pass. impers.: istuc mihi exquisitum est, fuisse hunc, etc.,I am accurately informed,: mi istuc primum exquisito est opus,I must first inquire respecting this,; cf. ; A. and S. Gr. § 243, R. 1: consilia exquirentes,.—Hence, ex-quīsītus, a, um, P. a., carefully sought out, ripely considered, choice, excellent, exquisite: ipsi omnia, quorum negotium est, consulta ad nos et exquisita deferunt,: reconditae exquisitaeque sententiae,: exquisitum judicium litterarum,: exquisitis rationibus confirmare,: summis ingeniis exquisitaque doctrina philosophi,: ars,: supplicia,: magistri,: munditia non odiosa neque exquisita nimis,too exquisite,: nihil elegans, nihil exquisitum,: epulae,. —Comp.: accuratius et exquisitius dicendi genus,: verba,.—Sup.: laudantur exquisitissimis verbis legiones,: ad exquisitissimam consuetudinem Graecorum aliquem erudire,: scientia exquisitissimae subtilitatis,.—

Sought out, ascertained, made certain: satin istuc mihi exquisitumst?.—Hence, adv.: exquīsīte, carefully, accurately, particularly, excellently, exquisitely: cum de eo crimine accurate et exquisite disputavisset,: eleganter atque exquisite dicere aliquid,.—Comp., ; ; .—Sup., Tiro Tull. ap. ; .

la:adj:exquisitissimus.gloss: sought out, searched for, hunted up, ascertained, having been sought out
